purpose: Ceftaroline fosamil is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including skin and soft tissue infections and a type of pneumonia called community-acquired bacterial pneumonia. It is often used when other antibiotics have not worked or when the infection is caused by tough bacteria like MRSA. Your doctor prescribes it to help your body fight off these infections and help you feel better.
how_it_works: This medicine works by attacking and breaking down the outer wall that bacteria need to survive. Without that protective wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. What makes this antibiotic special is that it can fight even resistant bacteria like MRSA, which many other antibiotics cannot handle.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, rash, itching, headache, dizziness, and low levels of potassium in your blood. You may also notice some redness or discomfort at the spot where the IV is given. Most side effects are mild, but let your care team know if anything bothers you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to any antibiotic, especially penicillins or cephalosporins, as you could have a serious allergic reaction to this medicine too. This antibiotic can sometimes cause a severe type of diarrhea called C. difficile infection, so let your doctor know right away if you develop bad or persistent diarrhea. It can also affect blood cell counts, so your doctor may do blood tests while you are being treated.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (into your vein) by a nurse or healthcare provider, usually in a hospital or infusion center. The typical adult dose is 600 mg given every 8 to 12 hours, depending on the type of infection being treated. Each dose is infused slowly over about 1 hour, and treatment usually lasts 5 to 14 days depending on how your infection responds.
